newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-CONTROVERSY AS AUSTRALIA FORGE AHEAD IN THIRD TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CONTROVERSY AS AUSTRALIA FORGE AHEAD IN THIRD TEST.

text.p: Umpiring controversy added to the tensions of a gripping third test on Saturday as Australia fought to extend their first innings lead of 73 over England.
At lunch on the third day they were 78 for three, a useful 151 ahead.
The talking point was the dismissal of Greg Blewett for 19, with the score 33 for one. He edged off-spinner Robert Croft to slip, where Nasser Hussain, falling forward, claimed a catch.
Blewett stood his ground and umpire Srivinas Venkataraghavan consulted his colleague George Sharp at square leg before raising his finger, to Blewett's obvious displeasure.
Repeated television replays, not available to the officials, failed to clarify whether the ball had touched the ground before Hussain got his fingers underneath it.
It was a welcome fillip to England and three overs later Matthew Elliott, having made 11, gave Mark Butcher his second catch off Dean Headley to leave the tourists at 39 for three.

The first catch had seen off Mark Taylor for only one -- his fourth failure in five test innings. The Australian captain was out in identical fashion to the first innings, squared up by Headley and edging to slip.
Headley, who had taken four for 72 in the first innings of his debut, rested with figures of two for 21. Mark Waugh (20) and his twin brother Steve (23 ) then steered Australia through to lunch.
Earlier, Shane Warne and Glenn McGrath needed only 22 balls to take the two remaining England wickets as play resumed in bright sunshine.
Andy Caddick (15) fell to Warne, whose final figures were six for 48. That took him ahead of fellow Australian Richie Benaud as the most successful leg-spinner in test history, with 249 victims.
McGrath wrapped up the innings with only one run added to the overnight score of 161 for eight when he yorked Headley for a duck.
